chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The expiation for omens (superstition) is reliance (upon Allah).'

key_terms.الطِّيَرَةِ: omen / superstition (taking good or bad signs from events)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for superstition or taking omens in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (as) conveys the Prophet’s teaching that Tawakkul (trust in Allah) serves as the expiation for Al-Tiyarah (superstition or taking omens). This establishes a direct theological link between cognitive reliance on external signs and spiritual reliance on the Divine, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis as the antidote to the anxiety of the pre-Islamic Jahiliyyah period. It underscores that true faith replaces the fear of arbitrary fate with confident submission to Allah’s will.

en.hubeali: H 14684 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuny, who has narrated:
Abu Abdullahasws says that the Rasool Allahsaww said: ‘The expiration of the omen is the reliance (upon Allahazwj)’.
en.sarwar: 236. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuny, who has narrated: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) says that the Rasool Allah (saww) said: ‘The expiration of the omen is the reliance (upon Allah (azwj))’.
